findings.proposed_change:
Add shared lemmas in BUAffineL2.lean, before `bu_affine_derivative_l2`, so both theorems can use them.

(A) A projection lemma, for any measure μ and nonnegative-valued f g h:
`lintegral_lt_top_of_add3 {f g h : α → ℝ≥0∞} (H : (∫⁻ z in S, f z + g z + h z) < ⊤) : (∫⁻ z in S, f z) < ⊤ ∧ (∫⁻ z in S, g z) < ⊤ ∧ (∫⁻ z in S, h z) < ⊤`.
Proof: three times `(lintegral_mono fun z => ...).trans_lt H`, with the `le_add_of_nonneg_*` chains currently written out in hDwL2/hD2L2/hDtL2. The `hL2` hypotheses are then `(lintegral_lt_top_of_add3 (hL2 S hS hSb)).1`, `.2.1` and `.2.2`.

(B) The assembly lemma, stated for `K` and the scaled derivative fields directly:
`bu_affine_derivative_sum_lt_top (τ scale) (Dw D2w Dtw) (K) (hmDw : AEStronglyMeasurable (buAffineDw τ scale Dw) (volume.restrict K)) (hmD2 : AEStronglyMeasurable (buAffineD2w τ scale D2w) (volume.restrict K)) (hDwK : (∫⁻ z in K, ‖scale • Dw (buAffinePoint τ scale z)‖ₑ ^ (2:ℝ)) < ⊤) (hD2K : … scale ^ 2 • D2w …) (hDtK : … scale ^ 2 • Dtw …) : (∫⁻ z in K, ‖buAffineDw τ scale Dw z‖ₑ ^ (2:ℝ) + ‖buAffineD2w τ scale D2w z‖ₑ ^ (2:ℝ) + ‖buAffineDtw τ scale Dtw z‖ₑ ^ (2:ℝ)) < ⊤`.
Proof sketch: move the current body of lines 86-148 into it. That is: build hmDw/hmD2 via the rpow ∘ enorm measurability, split the integral with `lintegral_add_left'` twice, rewrite with the three `funext … rfl` equalities, and finish with `ENNReal.add_lt_top`.

Rewritten uses:
- `bu_affine_derivative_l2` (hypotheses `hτ hscale hupper`, with `hSsub` kept): `obtain ⟨h1,h2,h3⟩ := fun S hS hSb => lintegral_lt_top_of_add3 (hL2 S (hSsub S hS) hSb)`, then `exact bu_affine_derivative_sum_lt_top τ scale Dw D2w Dtw K (hscaled.2.1.mono_set hKsub).aestronglyMeasurable (hscaled.2.2.1.mono_set hKsub).aestronglyMeasurable (bu_affine_l2_smul … hDwL2 K hKsub hKb) …`, with `hscaled` and the `hweakS` projections supplied exactly as now.
- `bu_affine_derivative_l2_interval` (hypotheses `hscale hscale1`, `hweak`, `hL2`): the same call, with `bu_affine_l2_smul_interval` and `bu_affine_weak_derivatives_interval` supplying the three finiteness facts and `hscaled`.

Each theorem body then shrinks to roughly 15 lines (apply lemma A, three `smul` calls, apply lemma B).
findings.benefit: About 60 lines of nontrivial measure-theoretic bookkeeping (measurability of the rpow of the enorm, splitting an ENNReal lintegral into three terms, scalar-field identification) would live in one lemma instead of two. The two theorems would then differ only in which weak-derivative and L² inputs they supply, and a fix to the energy functional needs one edit. A reader also sees directly that the interval version and the `[0,1]`-restricted version differ only in the time-restriction step.
